assets.name: Wash
assets.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept
Asset type: landscape 16:9 RPG aesthetic exploration, a genuine original hand-painted watercolor illustration.
Primary request: Paint a brooding municipal railway station in an elevated overhead three-quarter oblique/trimetric view, near-parallel projection, in unmistakable loose PHYSICAL WATERCOLOR and economical freehand ink. It should look like a skilled watercolorist's concept painting on cold-pressed paper, not a game screenshot, not photorealism, not a 3D render, not a texture filter. Allow irregular imperfect strokes and simplify all surfaces into broad pigment shapes. Deliberately LOW DETAIL.
Scene and composition: continuous flat grounded railway station floor fills whole frame, cutaway roof for clear overhead view. An upper pedestrian gallery with a black railing stretches along upper left; a staircase descends at center-left. Beneath left gallery is a little repair workbench with ONE person standing at it. In lower left, a worn wooden bench seats ONE person with a patterned cushion; beside it a tiny tea table and potted plant. A large concrete support pier occupies frame center with a small coffee dispenser and a small relay terminal attached to it. A THIRD small traveler stands a little right of center in front of a CLOSED glass pedestrian barrier running diagonally across mid-right. The right half contains parallel freight rails, two simple rectangular cargo containers on wagons and an overhead automated loading crane. These three people stay small relative to architecture, plausible consistent RPG scale. No other people.
Medium and mark-making: large translucent Payne's-gray washes and sepia washes bleeding into each other, deep pooled pigment stains, wet-on-wet granulation, occasional drybrush broken edges. Grey-tinted paper shows through a lighter walking floor as broad negative space. Machinery reduced to blocks of dark wash with only a few crooked selective thin ink contour marks. Rails are long sparse ink lines, containers simplified flat watercolor silhouettes; no bolts, repetitive ridges or mechanical microdetail. Keep some edges diffuse or entirely lost; no universally sharp geometric outlines. No smooth volumetric metal shading or glossy rendered surfaces. Image remains a painting in all areas including people and machinery.
Lighting and palette: very dark brooding civic space, slate/charcoal Payne's gray and dirty sepia, subdued gray paper walking paths. Tiny warm ochre-amber strokes indicate existing lamps by repairbench and pier, avoiding glow/bloom. Quiet melancholy, dark but legible.
Constraints: elevated oblique/trimetric continuous playfield; no cinematic lens, vanishing-point depth, horizon, floating island/diorama, frames, UI, typography, text, watermark, extra props, creatures or horror. New drawing composition with main anchors in exact described relative positions; freehand painterly economy takes priority over microscopic precision.
assets.observations: More materially painterly than six reference-edited variants: broad irregular pigment stains, less smooth metal shading and sharply reduced repetitive machinery detail. Major scene anchors retained: upper-left gallery/stair/workbench, lower-left seated bench figure/plant/tea/cushion, centralpier coffee/relay, traveler at mid-right barrier, rightfreightrails/containers/crane. Exactlythreepeople; repairer standing instead of round01 seated. Fine architecture and placement differ, gallery shortened/reconfigured, bench/tea/pier fixtures redrawn and simpler, train containers shifted, single broad crane gantry. Closed barrier is present but gate panel segmentation differs and glass less explicit. This is a new painting experiment, not exact compositional match. Some forms still rendered volumetrically, but loose pigment shapes dominate larger areas.
